steps.tx: A localized collection of amylase-rich fluid enclosed within a non-epithelialized wall of fibrous and granulation tissue is defined as a **pancreatic pseudocyst**. Pseudocysts arise predominantly as a sequela of acute pancreatitis or chronic pancreatitis following pancreatic duct disruption, and less commonly secondary to blunt abdominal trauma. Unlike true congenital or neoplastic cysts, histopathological examination confirms a complete absence of an internal epithelial lining.
steps.say: A pancreatic pseudocyst is an encapsulated collection of amylase-rich fluid lacking an epithelial lining, arising after pancreatitis or duct disruption.

vis.alt: Gross anatomical diagram of the pancreas showing relationships to the stomach, lesser sac, and common sites of pseudocyst formation.
vis.caption: Surgical anatomy of the pancreas: lesser sac relationships where pseudocysts typically mature against the posterior stomach. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Pathophysiologically, the pseudocyst begins as an acute peripancreatic fluid collection that fails to resorb. Over a period of four to six weeks, surrounding peritoneal and retroperitoneal structures, including the posterior gastric wall, transverse mesocolon, and parietal peritoneum, mount an intense inflammatory reaction. This reaction organizes into a dense, mature fibrous capsule capable of holding surgical sutures without tearing, termed mural **capsular maturation**.
steps.say: Capsular maturation requires four to six weeks, during which fibrous tissue forms a capsule strong enough to support surgical sutures.

nodes.label: Acute Peripancreatic Fluid Accumulates in Lesser Sac
Mature Non-Epithelial Fibrous Capsule Formed (> 4-6 Weeks)

steps.tx: Most small asymptomatic pseudocysts measuring under four to six centimetres resolve spontaneously without active intervention through gradual reabsorption. Indications for therapeutic drainage encompass persistent symptoms such as epigastric pain, early satiety from gastric outlet obstruction, common bile duct compression causing jaundice, rapid enlargement, or life-threatening complications such as infection, rupture, and pseudoaneurysm **haemorrhage**.
steps.say: Indications for draining a pseudocyst include pain, gastric outlet obstruction, jaundice, rapid expansion, infection, or vascular erosion.

points: No compression of adjacent hollow organs
Immature capsule (< 4 weeks from acute episode)

right.title: Intervention Required
points: Persistent epigastric pain or early satiety

steps.tx: Prior to undertaking any drainage procedure, contrast-enhanced computed tomography or magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography is mandatory to delineate the cyst relationship to the stomach and define ductal anatomy. Cyst fluid analysis obtained by fine-needle aspiration demonstrates extremely high amylase activity alongside low carcinoembryonic antigen levels, reliably excluding mucinous **cystic neoplasms** of the pancreas.
steps.say: Cyst fluid analysis reveals high amylase and low CEA levels, confirming a benign pseudocyst and ruling out mucinous cystic neoplasms.

steps.tx: The neatest escape for a mature pseudocyst is straight into the stomach it already leans against. **Cystogastrostomy** cuts a wide window between cyst and gastric lumen, letting pancreatic fluid drain internally where it belongs, nowadays often created endoscopically with ultrasound guidance and stents. Six weeks of wall maturation earns the cyst this option, because a friable early collection cannot hold a join. Imaging first excludes the impostors, varices in the wall and pseudoaneurysms in the fluid, either of which converts drainage into haemorrhage.
steps.say: Cystogastrostomy drains a mature pseudocyst internally into the stomach through a surgically or endoscopically made window.

steps.tx: When an intervention is required for a mature pseudocyst densely adherent to the posterior wall of the stomach, the definitive surgical procedure is open or laparoscopic **cystogastrostomy**. Through an anterior gastrotomy, the posterior gastric wall is incised into the adherent pseudocyst cavity, fluid and necrotic debris are evacuated, and the edges of the posterior stomach and cyst wall are sutured together circumferentially.
steps.say: Cystogastrostomy establishes internal drainage by creating an anastomosis between the pseudocyst and the adherent posterior gastric wall.

vis.alt: Surgical diagram showing posterior gastrotomy and creation of an internal anastomosis into a pancreatic pseudocyst.
vis.caption: Cystogastrostomy: internal anastomotic decompression of a mature lesser sac pseudocyst into the stomach lumen. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Historically described by Jurasz, surgical cystogastrostomy provides permanent dependent internal drainage because gastric acid promptly neutralizes pancreatic enzymes while the cyst cavity rapidly obliterates as it contracts. In contemporary practice, endoscopic ultrasound-guided cystogastrostomy has largely replaced open surgery. An expandable bifanged lumen-apposing metal stent or multiple double-pigtail plastic stents are deployed transmurally across the gastric wall into the cyst under real-time **endosonography**.
steps.say: Endoscopic ultrasound cystogastrostomy provides transmural stents between the stomach and pseudocyst under real-time ultrasound guidance.

nodes.label: EUS Localisation of Pseudocyst Abutting Posterior Stomach
Electrocautery Tract Dilation across Gastric Wall
Deployment of Lumen-Apposing Metal or Pigtail Stents

steps.tx: When a pseudocyst is located within the inframesocolic compartment or does not adhere to the posterior stomach wall, surgical cystogastrostomy is technically infeasible. For these lesions, surgical **cystojejunostomy** is executed, utilizing an isolated forty-to-fifty centimetre Roux-en-Y jejunal loop anastomosed to the most dependent portion of the cyst wall. External catheter drainage is strictly avoided for non-infected pseudocysts due to the high hazard of creating an intractable pancreaticocutaneous fistula.
steps.say: Pseudocysts non-adherent to the stomach are drained via Roux-en-Y cystojejunostomy, avoiding external drains that risk permanent fistulas.

rows: Pseudocyst adherent to posterior gastric wall

steps.tx: The most catastrophic vascular emergency complicating a pancreatic pseudocyst is the erosion of enzymatic secretions into an adjacent major artery, forming a **pseudoaneurysm**. The splenic artery is most commonly affected, followed by the gastroduodenal and superior mesenteric arteries. Sudden acute haemorrhage into the pseudocyst or gastrointestinal tract produces torrential bleeding, which demands immediate diagnostic angiography and emergency transcatheter arterial coil embolization.
steps.say: Enzymatic erosion of the splenic artery creates a pseudoaneurysm, which requires urgent transcatheter angiographic coil embolization.
